items.title: After COVID, biomanufacturing tackles preparedness and commercialization challenges
items.snippet: Manufacturers are redesigning their processes to balance both better future emergency vaccine mobilization and the more demanding work of maintaining flexible, commercially viable manufacturing networks.

items.title: Nektar prevails in legal battle with Lilly over broken rezpeg partnership
items.snippet: Nektar Therapeutics has been awarded $90 million in damages after a jury sided with the biotech, which had accused Big Pharma Eli Lilly of “botching” an analysis of their formerly partnered autoimmune drug.

items.title: ADARx raises $446M in biotech’s third largest IPO of 2026, City files to go public
items.snippet: Two RNA biotechs, ADARx Pharmaceuticals and City Therapeutics, are taking advantage of the IPO frenzy, which has led to a total of 27 newly public biotechs so far this year.

items.title: J&J, Legend tout long-term survival benefits for Carvykti in multiple myeloma
items.snippet: Ten patients out of 20 who received Johnson & Johnson and Legend Biotech’s Carvykti remained alive at five years of follow up.

items.title: Genentech makes $1.5B+ deal with AI heavyweight Earendil for cancer bispecifics
items.snippet: Genentech's agreement with Earendil Labs came the same day its parent company, Roche, inked a cardiometabolic and renal deal with Atavistik Bio for up to $2 billion.

items.title: FDA slams GLP-1 compounder over risk of contaminating drugs ‘with filth’
items.snippet: FDA inspectors found evidence that the compounding pharmacy was making versions of Eli Lilly’s tirzepatide and Novo’s semaglutide “regularly or in inordinate amounts” at a site with “insanitary conditions.”

items.title: US senators grill FDA nominee Overton on ability to ‘stand up’ to Trump
items.snippet: In Thursday’s Senate committee meeting, FDA commissioner nominee Heidi Overton was repeatedly questioned about her ability to retain the FDA’s independence under President Donald Trump, as well as about her views on vaccines and abortion drugs.

items.title: Acadia slides on Phase 2 miss in Alzheimer’s psychosis but keeps moving asset forward
items.snippet: While Acadia Pharmaceuticals’ candidate has missed the main goal of a Phase 2 trial, the company is still moving forward with the anti-psychosis candidate in Alzheimer’s disease as well as Lewy body dementia.

items.title: Merck’s experimental eye drug matches Roche’s VEGF inhibitor but safety concerns emerge
items.snippet: Analysts were keen to see a new modality compete with Roche’s approved drug Lucentis in the late-stage trial but new safety issues could complicate the future for Merck’s candidate.

items.title: Kyverna steps closer to FDA-first CAR T for an autoimmune condition with durability data
items.snippet: Kyverna Therapeutics' miv-cel showed improved mobility and a favorable safety profile at one year in patients with stiff person syndrome, further derisking an upcoming FDA application, William Blair said on Thursday. The biotech plans to file for priority review this year.

items.title: Eli Lilly’s weekly insulin shot cleared by FDA, setting up another front in Novo rivalry
items.snippet: The weekly insulin Onswik will now be available to U.S. patients after initial approvals in Europe, Mexico and Japan.

items.title: Backed by NVIDIA, Basecamp bags $140M to advance AI-designed drugs
items.snippet: Basecamp Research joins the growing group of AI-forward biotechs that in recent months have brought in notable sums from investors, including Isomorphic Labs and Enveda.

items.title: Roche inks up to $2B deal with Atavistik for new cardiometabolic drugs
items.snippet: The new partnership follows Roche’s recent R&D expansion in Boston focused on development for cardiovascular, renal and metabolic diseases.

items.title: Lilly sets aside up to $3.25B to tackle critical unmet need targets with InnoCare
items.snippet: InnoCare Pharma is the latest addition to Eli Lilly’s dealmaking spree, which includes some of the biggest acquisitions this year: up to $7 billion for Kelonia Therapeutics in April and up to $7.8 billion for Centessa Pharmaceuticals in March.

items.title: How radioligand therapy is rewriting cancer care
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured presented by Curium, Jennifer Smith-Parker speaks to Mike Patterson, CEO North America and Professor Sabine Brookman-May, vice president and head of Global Clinical Development. We look at the momentum behind radioligand therapy and how its diagnostic and therapeutic capabilities are impro...

items.title: The human cost of AI interviews
items.snippet: While artificial intelligence can help biotech and pharma companies more quickly vet job applicants, it can also turn off the very people they want to employ. Two recruiting experts discuss AI’s role and limitations in the hiring process.

items.title: Growth mode: 3 biotechs that are staffing up after series B raises
items.snippet: Biotechs that announced series B financing this year and are expanding their workforces include one that raised $2.1 billion and has partnerships with Eli Lilly, Johnson & Johnson and Novartis.

items.title: Immunovant ditches lupus for multi-hyphenate inflammatory drug after mid-stage miss
items.snippet: After imeroprubart failed to demonstrate sufficient efficacy in lupus during a Phase 2b trial, Immunovant is moving on from the indication and looking to other high priority programs for the drug in neurology, endocrinology and rheumatology.

items.title: AI drug hunter Enveda raises $311M for late-stage obesity, inflammatory disease push
items.snippet: Tech darling Enveda has raised a total of $845 million in the past six years. The latest funding round is intended to pave the way for an IPO someday.

items.title: Amgen asset from $27.8B Horizon buy scores in Phase 3 Sjögren's study
items.snippet: Amgen is awaiting another Phase 3 readout for the investigational Sjögren's disease therapy, set for later this year. William Blair anticipates that at least two trials will be needed to support an FDA application.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

items.title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
items.snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.
